- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially in early horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >80.0) are common; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak if sentiment is positive.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts often overreact to sentiment; dampen slope or reduce amplitude if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day starting from day 10.
